dublinCore.description: Interactive Bode plot of a first-order RC low-pass filter. Sliders set R and C through standard E12 values; the gain (dB) and phase (degrees) are plotted against log frequency from 1 Hz to 100 kHz, with the corner frequency fc = 1/(2 pi R C), the -3 dB and -45 degree points, the -20 dB/decade roll-off and the straight-line asymptotes.

learningObjectives: Calculate the time constant tau = RC and the corner frequency fc = 1/(2 pi R C) for given values of R and C
Identify the -3 dB gain and the -45 degree phase at the corner frequency on a Bode plot
Explain why the gain falls by 20 dB per decade and the phase approaches -90 degrees well above fc
Predict how changing R or C moves the Bode plot along the frequency axis without changing its shape
Select standard E12 values of R and C that place the corner frequency near a target frequency
prerequisites: Impedance of a resistor and a capacitor

misconceptions.misconception: The cutoff frequency is where the filter stops passing signals
misconceptions.correction: At fc the output amplitude is still 70.7% of the input (-3.01 dB) and at 2 fc it is 44.7% (-6.99 dB); the attenuation grows gradually
misconceptions.evidence: Hover just above the orange corner line and watch the gain read-out fall gradually

misconceptions.misconception: A larger resistor or capacitor raises the cutoff frequency
misconceptions.correction: fc = 1/(2 pi R C), so increasing R or C lowers fc
misconceptions.evidence: Move either slider to the right and the orange corner line moves to the left

misconceptions.misconception: The straight-line Bode sketch is the real response
misconceptions.correction: The exact gain is 3.01 dB below the asymptotes at fc and the phase differs by up to 5.7 degrees at fc/10 and 10 fc
misconceptions.evidence: Turn on the straight-line asymptotes and compare them with the curves near fc

accessibility.screenReaderScript: Bode plot of an RC low-pass filter. Two sliders set the resistance and the capacitance. The top plot shows the gain in decibels and the bottom plot the phase in degrees against frequency from 1 Hz to 100 kHz. The corner frequency, where the gain is -3 dB and the phase is -45 degrees, is marked and read out together with the time constant.

controls.label: Resistance R
controls.description: Index into the E12 resistor values from 10 ohm to 100 kohm (12 log-spaced values per decade); the label shows the resistance

controls.label: Capacitance C
controls.description: Index into the E12 capacitor values from 1 nF to 100 uF (12 log-spaced values per decade); the label shows the capacitance

controls.label: Show straight-line asymptotes
controls.description: Shows or hides the dashed straight-line Bode approximations of the gain and phase

visualElements.description: Gain plot: 20 log10 |H(f)| in dB against log frequency (red), with the -3 dB corner point, the -20 dB/decade slope triangle and optional asymptotes
Phase plot: angle of H(f) in degrees against log frequency (blue), with the -45 degree corner point and optional asymptotes
Circuit diagram of the RC low-pass filter labelled with the current R and C
Read-outs of the time constant tau = RC, the corner frequency fc and the gain and phase at the hover cursor

model.description: First-order RC low-pass transfer function evaluated on a logarithmic frequency grid

instructionalStrategies: Compare the exact response with the straight-line Bode sketch
Design with standard E12 component values
extensions: Add the matching RC high-pass filter and compare the two Bode plots
Cascade two RC sections and observe the -40 dB/decade roll-off
